## Overview

CEAT Discovery Day brings K–12 students to campus for a hands-on look at how the iHuman Lab builds technology that understands people — not just their commands, but their attention, stress, and mistakes before they happen. Students get an introduction to brain-computer interfaces, human-robot interaction, and eye-gaze AI, drawn from the lab's ongoing research in search-and-rescue robotics, aviation safety, manufacturing, and healthcare.

## What Students Will See

- **Brain-computer interfaces** — how brain signals can be read in real time to detect stress and workload
- **Human-robot teaming** — robots that adapt to the person operating them, including teleoperation over high-latency links
- **Eye-gaze AI** — training models to see the way expert operators do, from surgeons to drone pilots
- **Pathways into research** — how to get involved in human-centered AI and robotics research as a student

## Venue

Oklahoma State University, Stillwater, OK
